version.changelog: Initial release: review skills for token efficiency, scriptability, clearer action boundaries, and backup-first improvement flow.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: master-skill-review
Version: 1.0.0

This is a 'meta-skill' designed to audit and modify other OpenClaw skills. While its stated purpose is benign (optimizing token efficiency and scriptability), it explicitly requests elevated permissions to inspect and overwrite local files across different skill directories (SKILL.md, scripts/). The core script 'scripts/review_skill.sh' is a safe diagnostic tool, but the instructions in 'SKILL.md' directing the AI to autonomously 'improve' and modify other skills represent a high-risk capability for automated code manipulation that could be easily subverted, though no explicit malicious intent or data exfiltration was found.

llm.summary: The skill is a meta-reviewer that legitimately inspects local skill files, but its documentation promises backup-and-modify capabilities and elevated permissions that are not implemented in the shipped script—be cautious about granting write access or assuming it performs backups.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose (review other skills for verbosity, scriptability, and boundaries) matches the files the skill touches (SKILL.md, scripts/, references/). However, SKILL.md and README claim the tool will 'back up first, then modify' and requires 'higher local permissions' while the provided script only performs read-only inspection and reporting. This mismatch between claimed modify/backup behavior and actual code is an inconsistency (overpromise).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell an agent to inspect and potentially modify other local skill folders and to back up before modifying. The included script (scripts/review_skill.sh) only reads files, lists sizes, and emits heuristics — it does not implement backup or modification. The instruction-level claim that the skill may modify other skills is potentially sensitive because if an agent with this skill is later given filesystem write permissions, those instructions could lead to edits; currently the code does not perform network exfiltration or access unrelated system paths.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only plus a simple shell script) — low install risk. The shipped script is small, local, and uses only standard shell utilities; there are no downloads, external installers, or extracted archives.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The scope of required access (reading local skill files) is proportional to the stated review purpose. That said, the documentation's suggestion of elevated local permissions should be validated by the platform before granting write access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent or always-on privileges (always: false) and does not include autonomous-invocation restrictions. It declares a typical owner of a high-privilege 'master' agent; granting that agent filesystem write access would increase risk because the instructions encourage modifying other skills (even though the provided script is read-only).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This meta-skill appears to be a small, local reviewer tool and its script only reads and reports about a target skill directory (no network calls). However: (1) SKILL.md promises backup-and-modify behavior that is not implemented in scripts/review_skill.sh — do not assume automatic backups or safe edits; (2) only grant this skill (or the agent using it) read/write access if you trust it — prefer running the review script in a sandbox or read-only mode first; (3) if you want automated modification, require an explicit, auditable backup step and visible confirmation before any write; (4) verify platform-level permissions and logging so any file changes are recorded. If you need this installed, run the included script against a test copy of a skill folder to confirm actual behavior before giving it access to production skill folders.
